passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 1. Receiving a grievance Grievances are accepted from any channel: web form, messaging apps, email, phone, social media and walk-in at the office or a community worker. Every grievance gets a ticket number and an acknowledgement within 1 working day. The acknowledgement states the ticket number, the team that will handle it and the expected first response time. Beneficiaries never pay any fee to file a grievance.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 2. Emergencies A household is in crisis when it has no food today or nowhere to sleep tonight, when someone is being beaten or thrown out of their home, or when someone talks about suicide. These cases are alerted to the head of the Protection Unit at once and receive a first response within 2 hours. The officer may arrange emergency food support or temporary shelter while the underlying problem is solved. Late or missing aid alone is not an emergency; it is rated high or normal.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 3. Benefit not received or late When a payment has not arrived, the officer checks within 72 hours: (a) whether the person is on the current beneficiary list, (b) the payment status for this period, and (c) whether the card or account is active. If the payment failed for a technical reason, the officer files a correction with the payment agency and tells the beneficiary the new expected date. If several beneficiaries in the same area report the same missing payment, the Benefits Team checks the batch as a whole.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 4. Registration and eligibility People who believe they are eligible but are not registered can ask for an assessment. The officer explains the documents needed (identity document, household card or proof of residence, and proof of income where required) and books a home visit by a community worker within 14 days. Eligibility decisions follow the programme rules; officers do not promise that a person will be accepted. Wrong data, such as a deceased member or a wrong address, is corrected in the registry within 14 days.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 5. Payment schedule and pickup Payment dates and pickup points are published each period. The officer gives the published schedule and the nearest pickup point. A beneficiary who cannot travel because of age, disability or illness can authorise a family member in writing to collect on their behalf.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 6. Disability and elderly services Requests for assistive devices, home care or a disability assessment go to the Social Rehabilitation Team. A first contact happens within 72 hours. Elderly people living alone without care are rated high and visited within 7 days.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 7. Suspected fraud, illegal fees or deductions Beneficiaries must receive their full entitlement. Any fee, cut, forced purchase or deduction by an agent, shop or official is prohibited. The Payment Oversight Team investigates reports within 7 days and protects the identity of the person reporting. Repeated reports about the same agent or shop trigger an audit of that agent.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 8. Replying to the beneficiary Replies are written in the beneficiary's language, in plain words. They acknowledge the specific problem, give the ticket number and the expected first response time in hours, and never promise that aid will be paid. Personal data such as identity numbers and card numbers is not repeated. Every reply drafted by software must be reviewed and approved by an officer before it is sent.

passages.title: Sample SOP: social assistance grievance handling (written for this demo, replace with your agency's own)
passages.text: 9. Closing a grievance A grievance is closed when the problem is solved or a clear decision with reasons has been given, and the beneficiary has been informed. The beneficiary may appeal a decision within 30 days. Grievance statistics are reported to leadership every month, without personal data.
